summary:
Wang–Lau–Zhou (arXiv 2601.08111) derandomize matrix concentration by replacing the classical conditional expectation E[f(X)|fixed part] with the free potential Φ(t,x)=tr⊗τ(f(A_0⊗1 + A(x)⊗1 + √(1−t)·X̄_free)), where X̄_free=Σ A_i⊗s_i is the semicircular linear pencil (eq. (5) p.2, Def. 2.23 p.17, mixed operator p.7, footnote 3 p.8). Everything they compute is an (operator-valued) EXPECTATION of an even functional: moments via the non-crossing recursion of Lemma 6.1 (p.57), resolvents via the re-centred power series of Lemma 6.3/Cor. 6.4 (p.58–59), and the replacement error per step is the "expectation pushed inside" difference of eq. (10) (p.3) bounded by intrinsic freeness, Prop. 3.24 (p.28): Σ_k |E tr⊗τ(Y X^k Y X^{2p−2−k}) − tr(Y φ[X^k] Y φ[X^{2p−2−k}])| ≲ p^3 σ(X)ν(X)σ(Y)ν(Y) tr⊗τ(X^{2p−4}); accumulated over the walk this gives Theorem 4.2 (p.33): ‖A_0+A(x)‖_{2p} ≤ ‖A_0⊗1+√K X̄_free‖_{2p} + O(p^{3/4}√(σν)). The paper contains no Dyson equation; Lemma 6.1 is its power-series form and I checked numerically (residual 1.6e-16) that resumming it gives G(z)=φ[(z−X)^{-1}]=(z−A_0−Σ_i A_i G A_i)^{-1}.

For our problem the verdict is negative and exact. (a) Odd functionals: the free Wick formula (Thm 2.30 p.18) sums only non-crossing PAIR partitions, so τ of any monomial odd in the centred free part is identically 0; our hub pairing (TA_b∘T)(TC_b)^T and in fact EVERY term of the κ3 readout (coherent, cross, diagonal, bulk of Prop. parts in sec_transport.tex) is cubic in W_l, hence has exact mean zero over W_l and free prediction exactly zero (PROVED: odd moment of a centred Gaussian / only pair partitions). The paper's own method never computes such terms: the pairwise-independent update "only depends on the first and second order statistics" (p.8) and the cubic terms are the Taylor remainder R_m bounded in (27) p.37. (b) Partial conditioning: the exact Gaussian conditional expectation of the pairing given W_l's action on a k-dimensional subspace (W_∥=W_lΠ) has the closed form E[P_ij|W_∥]=Σ_r (W_∥GC_b)_{jr}[(W_∥GA_b)_{ir}(W_∥G)_{ir} + (2/n)(A_b^TG^T(I−Π)G)_{rr}] for i≠j plus two more Wick terms on the diagonal (PROVED; CHECKED against Monte Carlo to the noise level, 0.019 vs 0.019 at k=64). The off-diagonal energy it explains is ≈ (leg-energy fraction captured)^3, and the cocycle-adapted subspace is no better than a random one inside range(G) (CHECKED, n=256, age 3: legE 0.52/0.77/0.96/0.998 → explained 0.16–0.18/0.47–0.51/0.90/0.994, vs legE^3 0.14/0.46/0.89/0.993). Since the conditional mean is the MSE-optimal estimator from that information, no free- or classical-conditional-expectation readout from a rank-k summary of W_l can recover the bulk: to hold the slice energy to 1e-6 one needs 1−legE ≈ 3e-7, i.e. full rank (the gate makes rank(T)=n/2 exactly; k=n/2 gives 100%). This is F2/F3 restated as an information bound. (c) Scale: the pairing is a finite-width fluctuation: rms_off(P)/rms_off(T S_b T^T) = 0.15/√n for n=64..512 (CHECKED), the n^{-1/2} order of odd cumulants; its W_l-mean over M resamples is |mean|/|typical| = 1/√M exactly (0.0708 vs 0.0707; 0.1416 vs 0.1414), i.e. pure noise around zero. The intrinsic-freeness parameters of a He-initialised layer are σ(W)=√2, ν(W)=σ_*(W)=√(2/n), so σν=2/√n: the error of replacing anything by its free model is the SAME order n^{-1/2} as the memory the chain exists to carry. (d) The Gaussian covariance recursion C_{l+1}=E[relu relu^T](W_lC_lW_l^T) is a realization-specific congruence followed by an entrywise (arc-cosine) nonlinearity; it is not a linear-pencil resolvent and not a Dyson fixed point. Its ensemble average collapses, because for W=Σ_{ab}√(2/n)g_{ab}E_{ab} the covariance map is Σ_i A_iMA_i=(2/n)tr(M)I (PROVED), to the scalar NNGP recursion — the free model of a Gaussian layer costs O(1) per moment and carries no realization. What IS free-multiplicative is the cocycle's spectrum: τ((TT^T)^k) matches the free product formulas of a=W^TW and b=GG^T to 1–2% at n=256 and <1% at n=1024 (CHECKED), which is the origin of the effective-rank numbers of sec_cost.tex; that is a statement about the transport, not about the Hadamard readout. Net: the paper supplies no mechanism that evaluates, compresses, or regenerates a realization-specific mean-zero odd functional; it supplies the vocabulary (σ, ν, σ_*, Prop. 3.24) that quantifies exactly why the free/ensemble replacement loses it.

mechanisms.name: Operator-valued free model and its moment recursion (Dyson equation)
mechanisms.statement: Free model X_free = A_0⊗1 + Σ_{i=1}^n A_i⊗s_i with s_i free standard semicirculars (eq. (5) p.2; Def. 2.23 p.17); partial trace φ=Id_d⊗τ (Sec. 2.2.3 p.17). Lemma 6.1 (p.57): φ[X^p] = φ[X^{p−1}]A_0 + Σ_i Σ_{k=0}^{p−2} φ[X^k] A_i φ[X^{p−2−k}] A_i, and the two-sided version φ[X^p(B⊗1)X^q]; proved from the first-order free integration by parts (Cor. 6.6 p.60) plus Lemma 2.32 (p.19) φ[XYXZ]=φ[X(φ[Y]⊗1)X]φ[Z]. Resumming G(z)=Σ_p φ[X^p]/z^{p+1} gives the operator-valued Dyson/subordination equation G=(z−A_0−η(G))^{-1}, η(G)=Σ_i A_iGA_i. The paper never writes the Dyson equation (grep: no 'Dyson', 'fixed point', 'subordination'); it only uses the recursion as a dynamic programme (Lemma 6.2 p.57: O(pq) subproblems, each a sum of n products of d×d matrices).
mechanisms.status: PROVED (paper: Lemma 6.1, Cor. 6.6, Lemma 2.32). CHECKED: resummed series satisfies the Dyson equation with residual 1.6e-16 (d=6, 5 coefficient matrices, 400 moments) and equals the fixed-point iterate to 1.6e-16.
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: For our W_l = Σ_{ab}√(2/n)g_{ab}E_{ab} the covariance map is η(M)=Σ_{ab}(2/n)E_{ab}ME_{ba}=(2/n)tr(M)I, so the free model of a Gaussian layer is a scalar (the NNGP/mean-field recursion). The recursion is cheap precisely because it carries no realization; F1's 12n^3 per source-age is the price of the realization.

mechanisms.name: Intrinsic-freeness parameters σ, ν, σ_* and their values for a He layer
mechanisms.statement: Def. 2.35 (p.20): σ(X)^2 = max{‖φ[X̄^*X̄]‖, ‖φ[X̄X̄^*]‖} = max{‖ΣA_iA_i^*‖,‖ΣA_i^*A_i‖}; ν(X)^2 = ‖Cov(X)‖ = ‖Σ vec(A_i)vec(A_i)^*‖; σ_*(X)^2 = sup_{‖u‖=‖v‖=1} Σ_i (u^*A_iv)^2; σ_* ≤ min(σ,ν). Thm 4.1 (p.33, = [BBvH23, Thm 2.7]): |E‖X‖_{2p} − ‖X_free‖_{2p}| ≤ 2p^{3/4}σ^{1/2}ν^{1/2}; eq. (12) p.3: spec(X) ⊆ spec(X_free)+C σ^{1/2}ν^{1/2}(log d)^{3/4}+α w.p. 1−e^{−α^2}. For W with i.i.d. N(0,2/n) entries (Hermitised if needed): σ=√2, ν=√(2/n), σ_*=√(2/n), so σν = 2/√n and the free-replacement error is O(n^{-1/4}) on the edge, O(n^{-1/2}) in σν-units.
mechanisms.status: PROVED (direct evaluation of Def. 2.35: ΣA_iA_i^T = (2/n)·n·I = 2I; each entry has variance 2/n; Σ_{ab}(u_a v_b)^2·2/n = 2/n).
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: σν = 2/√n is the same order as the odd (κ3) fluctuations the chain carries (F2, F4: the slices are n^{-1/2}-type residuals). Any free/ensemble replacement therefore discards exactly the order of effect that separates the exact chain (3.5e-8) from the Gaussian closure; it cannot be used as a cheaper model of a fixed realization.

mechanisms.name: Free potential as a replacement for the classical conditional expectation, and its controlled error
mechanisms.statement: Mixed operator A_t(x)=A_0⊗1+A(x)⊗1+√(1−t)X̄_free (p.7), A(x)=Σx_iA_i; potential Φ(t,x)=tr⊗τ(A_t(x)^{2p})^{2/p} (Sec. 4.2 p.34). A_0(0)=X_free, A_1(g)=X. Footnote 3 (p.8): 'a geometric version of the method of conditional expectation ... √(1−t)X_free is an infinite dimensional approximation of the random matrix √(1−t)Σ A_ig_i, which captures the randomness that has yet to be derandomized. The tr⊗τ operator then approximates the expectation over this randomness.' Step: Φ(t+η/n, x+√η y) − Φ(t,x) = [tr⊗τ(X_{t,η}+√ηA(y))^{2p}]^{2/p} − [tr⊗τ(X_{t,η}+√(Kη/n)X̄'_free)^{2p}]^{2/p} (eq. (26) p.36), both Taylor-expanded to second order (Lemma 3.14); the free term's first-order part vanishes and its second-order part is Σ_i tr(A_iφ[X^k]A_iφ[X^{2p−2−k}]) by Lemma 2.32 — this is the expectation 'pushed inside' of eq. (10) (footnote 6 p.37); the deterministic term's second-order part is y^T∇^2φ(0)y/2p, and y is taken in the subspace H' orthogonal to ∇φ(0) and the top n/K eigenspace of the Hessian (p.37–38), which by Markov bounds it by (K/n)·Tr∇^2φ(0). The residual is the crossing-term difference bounded by Prop. 3.24 (p.28): ≲ p^3 ν̃(X)^2ν̃(Y)^2 tr⊗τ(X^{2p−4}), ν̃^2=σν, proved by Gaussian approximation (Thm 2.21, Cor. 2.27 p.16–18) + Gaussian covariance identity (Lemma 3.16) + [BBvH23] Lemma 3.22. Prop. 4.3 (p.34): Φ(t+η/n, x+√η y) ≤ Φ(t,x) + O((η/n)p^3σ^2ν^2) for y∈H', dim H' ≥ (ε+δ)n+2; third-order remainder R_m(H) ≲ p^2(‖X‖_{2p}^3‖H‖+‖H‖^4) (eq. (27) p.37). Total: Thm 4.2 (p.33). The update needs only first and second moments of dx_t ('the update formula only depends on the first and second order statistics of the entries of dx_t', p.8), so pairwise-independent y suffices. Resolvent version: Φ_z(t,x)=tr⊗τ|z1−A_t(x)|^{−2p} (eq. (28) p.43), Prop. 5.2 (p.43): |E_y Δ_z| ≲ η(p^3σ^2ν^2/Im z^5 + p(σ_*σ+σ_*^2r)/Im z^3), with multiplicative-weight aggregation over a net of z (Sec. 5.2).
mechanisms.status: PROVED in the paper (Prop. 4.3, Thm 4.2, Prop. 3.24, Prop. 5.2); proofs skimmed, structure verified against Lemma 2.32 and eq. (10).
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: The mechanism selects a realization x by minimizing an EVEN potential of the not-yet-fixed randomness; it evaluates nothing about a given realization that is odd in the remaining randomness — such terms are exactly the Taylor remainder (27). Our task is the opposite (evaluate a given W), so the method does not apply; what transfers is only the error calculus (σν per unit of replaced mass).

mechanisms.name: Cost of free moments and resolvents at resolution ε
mechanisms.statement: Lemma 6.2 (p.57): tr⊗τ((B_1⊗1)X^p(B_2⊗1)X^q) by dynamic programming over O(pq) subproblems φ[X^k], φ[X^k(B⊗1)X^l], each a sum over the n coefficient matrices of d×d products: O(pq·n·d^3) arithmetic (not stated as a count; follows from Lemma 6.1). Lemma 6.3 (p.58): for Y ≥ 0, ‖Y‖ ≤ u, tr⊗τ((ε^21+Y)^{−p}) to additive error δ by re-centring at u1−Y: Σ_k C(p+k−1,k) tr⊗τ((u1−Y)^k)/(ε^2+u)^{k+p}, truncated at k ≥ (2(u+ε^2)/ε^2) ln(4(ε^2+u)/(δε^2)), time O(k T(k)). Cor. 6.4 (p.59): tr⊗τ|z1−X|^{−2p} for z=λ+iε (and z=λ_max+ε real) in poly(‖A_0‖, σ(X), d, λ, p, 1/ε^2, log 1/δ) with u = 2λ^2+2(‖A_0‖+2σ)^2 from Pisier (Thm 2.24 p.17). Lehner's formula (Thm 2.25 p.17): ‖X_free‖ = inf_{Y≻0} max_± λ_max(±A_0+Y^{-1}+ΣA_i^*YA_i).
mechanisms.status: PROVED (paper); cost exponent in 1/ε^2 is read off the truncation index k.
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: Resolution ε enters as 1/ε^2 moments, each costing n·d^3 — for a d=n layer with n^2 Gaussian coefficients this would be n^5 per moment unless the covariance map collapses, which for i.i.d. W it does ((2/n)tr(M)I). So the free machinery is either trivial (ensemble, scalar) or far above the 12.8n^3 floor of F1; there is no intermediate regime that encodes a realization cheaply.

mechanisms.name: Free prediction for the hub-diagonal cubic pairing: exactly zero; what partial conditioning recovers
mechanisms.statement: (i) Free Wick formula, Thm 2.30 (p.18): φ[X_1⋯X_n] = Σ_{π∈NC_2[n]} φ_π — non-crossing PAIR partitions only, so φ of any product with an odd number of centred free factors is 0; Lemma 2.31 (p.18) adds index consistency. (ii) Our readout (kprop3.py slices_from_legs; sec_transport.tex Prop. parts): every part — coherent λ^2[2(a∘b)a^T+(a∘a)b^T], cross, diagonal (T∘T)D_{R_3}T^T, bulk (TA_b∘T)(TC_b)^T+… — is a cubic form in T=W_lG, hence cubic in the centred Gaussian W_l; E_{W_l}[·]=0 for all of them (third moment of a centred Gaussian vector), and the free model gives 0 for the same reason. So 'the bulk pairing is mean-zero' (F2) is true of the entire κ3 memory; what distinguishes the bulk is only that its realization needs n^3 numbers. (iii) The free potential at t<1 contains only terms even in X̄_free; an odd functional can only become nonzero when every variable it involves is in the fixed part A(x) — at which point it is the realized functional, computed at full cost. (iv) Partial information: with W_l = W_lΠ + W_l(I−Π), Π a rank-k orthogonal projector, the exact Gaussian conditional expectation is E[P_ij | W_lΠ] = Σ_r (W_∥GC_b)_{jr}[(W_∥GA_b)_{ir}(W_∥G)_{ir} + (2/n)(A_b^TG^T(I−Π)G)_{rr}] for i≠j (row j independent of row i kills every term with a W_⊥ factor in leg 3; Wick pairs legs 1,2 in row i), plus on the diagonal the Wick pairs (1,3),(2,3): (2/n)[(W_∥G)_{ir}(A_b^TG^T(I−Π)GC_b)_{rr} + (W_∥GA_b)_{ir}(G^T(I−Π)GC_b)_{rr}]. The first term is the coherent/cross structure of Prop. parts restricted to the known directions; the Wick terms are hub-diagonal contractions (diagonal-κ3-type). The conditional mean is the MSE-optimal estimator from that information. Measured explained energy of the off-diagonal pairing ≈ legE(k)^3, legE = ‖ΠG‖_F^2/‖G‖_F^2, for both random and cocycle-adapted subspaces; 1−explained ≈ 3(1−legE) near full capture.

mechanisms.status: PROVED: (i)–(iii) and the closed form (iv). CHECKED: closed form vs Monte Carlo over W_⊥ (n=256, age 3, M=300): off-diag |E−MC|/|E| = 0.058 at k=32 (noise 0.057), 0.019 at k=64 (noise 0.019); diagonal 0.043 (0.041), 0.016 (0.015). The law 'explained ≈ legE^3' is an empirical fit (10–30% high at small k from the Wick cross term), not a theorem.
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: F2 (bulk pairing is realization-specific, mean zero): confirmed and sharpened — all κ3 parts are mean-zero; the coherent/cross/diagonal parts are what survives conditioning on few directions, which is why reading old sources through them 'recovers almost nothing'. F3 (not regenerable from current statistics, subspace readouts fail): the best estimator from rank-k knowledge of W_l explains legE^3 of the energy, cocycle-adapted no better than random for the law; to reach the 1e-3 slice accuracy of F6 one needs 1−legE ≈ 3e-7, i.e. the full rank n/2 of the gated cocycle. F4 (sketches of the hub index have zero mean on trilinear forms): same odd-moment mechanism.

mechanisms.name: Fluctuation scale of the pairing and the n^{-1/2} law
mechanisms.statement: With bulk birth matrices of off-diagonal size O(n^{-1/2}) (the natural scale of off-diagonal pre-activation correlations) and He-scaled W, the pair-type transported object (TS_bT^T)_{ij} is O(n^{-1/2}) while the cubic pairing P_ij = Σ_r (TA_b)_{ir}T_{ir}(TC_b)_{jr} is a sum of n terms of size n^{-3/2} with random signs, O(n^{-1}); ratio ∝ n^{-1/2}. The W_l-mean of P is zero; its empirical mean over M resamples is pure noise.
mechanisms.status: CHECKED (age 3, Bernoulli(1/2) gates): rms_off(P)/rms_off(TS_bT^T) = 0.0186, 0.0132, 0.0095, 0.0063 at n = 64, 128, 256, 512, i.e. ratio·√n = 0.149, 0.149, 0.152, 0.142; |mean_M P|_F/|P|_F = 0.0707, 0.0708, 0.0708 (M=200, 1/√M=0.0707) and 0.1416 (M=50, 1/√M=0.1414). Heuristic scaling argument PROVED at the level of counting; absolute constants depend on the synthetic birth scale.
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: The memory is the first finite-width (odd, n^{-1/2}) correction to the Gaussian/mean-field closure, exactly the order that σν=2/√n says the free model misses. It is not a small part of a large object that could be bounded away: F4's 'slices are ~3% residuals of O(1) objects needed to 1e-2' is this n^{-1/2} (1/√1024 = 3.1%).

mechanisms.name: Gaussian covariance recursion vs operator-valued Dyson fixed point; the cocycle spectrum
mechanisms.statement: The chain's Gaussian part C_{l+1} = E_{z~N(Wμ, WC_lW^T)}[relu(z)relu(z)^T] (kprop3.py linear_step + nonlin_step) is a congruence by the fixed realization W_l followed by an entrywise nonlinear map of (S_ii,S_jj,S_ij); it is a forward dynamical system, not a resolvent of a linear pencil, and no self-consistent (Dyson) equation holds for a fixed realization. Its ensemble average over W_l is the scalar NNGP map because η(M)=(2/n)tr(M)I; fluctuations of C_{l+1} about it are the realization-specific O(n^{-1/2}) off-diagonal structure. What does obey free multiplicative convolution is the squared-singular-value law of the cocycle T=W_lD_{l-1}⋯: with a=W_l^TW_l and b=GG^T (G=D_{l-1}T_{l-1←l'}), by unitary invariance of Ginibre W_l the moments are τ(TT^T)=τ(a)τ(b), τ((TT^T)^2)=τ(a^2)τ(b)^2+τ(a)^2τ(b^2)−τ(a)^2τ(b)^2 (free product), with a → 2·Marchenko–Pastur(1): τ(a)=2, τ(a^2)=8.
mechanisms.status: PROVED (collapse of η for i.i.d. W; asymptotic freeness of Ginibre from deterministic matrices is standard, not in this paper). CHECKED: n=1024, ages 2/3/4: m1 = 0.958/1.014/0.920 vs free 0.956/1.015/0.918; m2 = 4.71/7.14/7.78 vs free(a=2MP) 4.68/7.18/7.67 (≤1.5%); n=256 within 2%. Effective ranks ‖T‖_F^2/s_1^2 = 92.6/67.7/47.2 at n=1024 for Bernoulli gates, same order as the real network's 92/65/47 at ages 2/3/4.
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: F1/F3: the cocycle's contraction (Oseledets/effective-rank numbers) is an ensemble, free-probabilistic fact and is well predicted; the Hadamard readout is not a trace of a polynomial in T and is invisible to it. F7 (collective mode): the top singular direction of the product is the one object the ensemble theory does describe (rank-1 part of the free product), consistent with the coherent part being cheap.

mechanisms.name: Traffic/graph extensions of free probability (literature remark, not in the paper)
mechanisms.statement: Hadamard products, diagonal extraction and transposes are 'traffic' operations (Male, traffic distributions); for unitarily invariant ensembles the large-n limit of E of such graph functionals is computable by cactus/graph sums, but it is still an ENSEMBLE expectation, and for a functional of odd degree in a centred Gaussian matrix it is zero by the same parity argument. No deterministic (non-averaged) evaluation of a Hadamard pairing at a fixed realization is provided by any such extension.
mechanisms.where: not in 2601.08111 (no mention of Hadamard products or traffics in the text); stated from the literature
mechanisms.status: CONJECTURE in the sense that I did not verify a reference text here; the parity statement is PROVED.
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: Closes the loophole 'maybe a richer free framework handles the Hadamard obstruction': any averaging framework returns 0 for the bulk pairing.

numerical_checks.what: Resummed Lemma 6.1 moment series satisfies the operator-valued Dyson equation G=(z−A_0−ΣA_iGA_i)^{-1} (d=6, 5 coefficients, z=4+i, 400 moments)
Hub pairing P=(TA_b∘T)(TC_b)^T, age-3 gated Ginibre cocycle, Bernoulli(1/2) gates: W_l-mean over M resamples and rms relative to the pair-type object TS_bT^T, n=64..512
Closed-form conditional expectation E[P | W_lΠ_k] (Π_k = top-k left singular subspace of G) vs Monte Carlo over W_⊥ (n=256, age 3, M=300)
numerical_checks.result: k=32: off-diag |E−MC|/|E| = 0.058 (MC noise 0.057), diag 0.043 (0.041); k=64: 0.019 (0.019), 0.016 (0.015). Formula confirmed at noise level. rank(G)=127=n/2 (gate), so k=n/2 explains 100%.

numerical_checks.what: Explained off-diagonal energy of P by E[P|W_lΠ_k] vs leg energy captured legE(k)
Free multiplicative convolution moments of the cocycle: τ(TT^T), τ((TT^T)^2) vs free-product formulas with a=W^TW (empirical and a=2·MP(1)), b=GG^T

caveats: (1) The paper has no Dyson equation and no Hadamard products; the Dyson resummation, the asymptotic freeness of Ginibre from deterministic matrices, and the traffic-probability remark are standard free-probability facts stated from my own knowledge, with the first two checked numerically here. (2) Numerics use synthetic ingredients: gates Bernoulli(1/2) independent of W (real relu gates are correlated with the weights and the input law), birth matrices S_b with i.i.d. O(n^{-1/2}) off-diagonal entries and O(1) gate coefficients; absolute scales (e.g. the 0.15/√n constant) are not those of the real networks, only the scaling laws and the zero-mean/conditional-mean structure transfer. I did not run on W_off0.npy. (3) The law 'explained ≈ legE^3' is an empirical fit at n=256 (deviations 10–30% at small k from the Wick cross term, <1% near full capture); the information-theoretic reading (conditional mean is MSE-optimal) assumes a Gaussian prior on W_l, i.e. it bounds estimators that use only a rank-k summary of W_l plus ensemble knowledge, not estimators that use W_l fully but compress something else. (4) The conditional-expectation framing conditions on W_l's action on k directions of range(G); the project's subspace readouts truncate the transported legs instead — related but not identical, so the legE^3 law is an idealized ceiling for that family, not a measurement of it. (5) The mean-zero statement applies to every part of the κ3 readout, not only the bulk; F2's wording should be read as 'the bulk is the part whose realization needs n^3 numbers', which the conditional-mean formula makes precise (coherent/cross/diagonal = what survives conditioning on few directions). (6) Proofs in Sections 4.3, 5.3, 7 were skimmed, not re-derived; equation numbers and pages are from the text dump and may be off by one page at page boundaries.
